Wait — should this be a model_family? The certificate lists multiple type designations. The schema says model_family: include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. Here there are 10 types listed. But the characteristics are given as a single set (Max = 272 kg, e ≥ 0.1 kg, etc.) applying to all. Hmm. The rule says include model_family only if cert covers >1 model variant. The types are 10 variants but the characteristics don't vary per model in the document. I could include model_family with the 10 models listed. Actually the certified_type.type_designations would include all. Should model_family be included? The instruction: "model_family: include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant". It covers 10 types. But we don't have per-model attributes. I think listing models in model_family with just model_id is reasonable. But it could also be fine to just list type_designations. Hmm.

The R60 example shows model_family being created even when the only distinguishing attribute is Emax. Here, types are distinct designations. I'll include model_family with family_name null and models for each type designation. Actually, let me reconsider — model_family might imply variants of a family; here the types are the certified types. I'll include it since >1 model variant. The models: 752KG, 753KG, 599KG, 597KG, 600KG, 752KGWA, 753KGWA, 599KGWA, 597KGWA, 600KGWA.

Divisions is a counting unit. I'll use "div" or "divisions". Keep raw: "divisions". Or maybe unit_symbol null since it's dimensionless count. I think "divisions" is fine as raw symbol. Let me use "divisions".
